```{r res-setup, include = FALSE}
hl_main <- c(0, 0.5, 1)
designs <- c('CO', 'Hybrid', 'OLBDC')
nr <- bench$null_rej
n_reps_main <- meta$n_reps
n_fit <- sum(cs$n_reps[cs$method %in% c('E2', 'E2cr2')])
n_conv <- sum(cs$n_conv[cs$method %in% c('E2', 'E2cr2')])
nrng <- function(method, d = designs, h = hl_main) {
  v <- nr$power[nr$method == method & nr$design %in% d & nr$t1half %in% h]
  sprintf('%s to %s', f3(min(v)), f3(max(v)))
}
krng <- function(method, d = designs) {
  v <- cs$kappa[cs$method == method & cs$design %in% d &
                  cs$t1half %in% hl_main]
  sprintf('%s to %s', f2(min(v)), f2(max(v)))
}
power_table <- function(method, caption, label) {
  s <- cs[cs$method == method & cs$t1half %in% hl_main, ]
  lines <- c('\\begin{table}[H]', '\\small\\centering',
             sprintf('\\caption{%s}', caption),
             sprintf('\\label{tab:%s}', label),
             '\\begin{tabular}{llrrr}', '\\toprule',
             '& & \\multicolumn{3}{c}{$c_{bm,B}$ (correlation channel)} \\\\',
             '\\cmidrule(l){3-5}',
             'Design, $t_{1/2}$ & $c_{bm,A}$ & 0 & 0.225 & 0.45 \\\\',
             '\\midrule')
  for (d in designs) for (h in hl_main) {
    for (a in c(0, 0.225, 0.45)) {
      vals <- vapply(c(0, 0.225, 0.45), function(b) {
        r <- s[s$design == d & s$t1half == h &
                 abs(s$c_bm_a - a) < 1e-9 & abs(s$c_bm_b - b) < 1e-9, ]
        sprintf('%s (%s)', f3(r$power), f3(r$mcse_power))
      }, character(1))
      lab <- if (a == 0) sprintf('%s, %s', dname(d), h) else ''
      lines <- c(lines, sprintf('%s & %s & %s \\\\', lab,
                                sprintf('%.3f', a),
                                paste(vals, collapse = ' & ')))
    }
    if (!(d == 'OLBDC' && h == 1)) lines <- c(lines, '\\addlinespace')
  }
  c(lines, '\\bottomrule', '\\end{tabular}', '\\end{table}')
}
cv <- function(d, h, n, m = 'E2') sprintf('%s (%s)', f3(ctr(d, h, n, m)),
                                          f3(ctr(d, h, n, m, 'mcse')))
crng <- function(n, d = designs, h = hl_main, m = 'E2') {
  r <- bench$contrasts
  v <- r$value[r$contrast == n & r$design %in% d & r$t1half %in% h &
                 r$method == m]
  sprintf('%s to %s', f3(min(v)), f3(max(v)))
}
ev <- bench$est_vs_analytic
cor_cells <- cs$method == 'E2' & cs$c_bm_a == 0 & cs$c_bm_b > 0 &
  cs$t1half %in% hl_main
cor_dev <- max(abs(cs$mean_est[cor_cells] /
                     (-cs$c_bm_b[cor_cells] * sd_br / sd_bm) - 1))
ev_main <- ev[ev$t1half %in% hl_main, ]
sd_ratio <- ev_main$sd_est / ev_main$se_gls
over_sim <- function(d, h) {
  cell(d, h, 0.45, 0, 'E2', 'mean_est') / -nominal - 1
}
cl <- bench$carry_loss
loss <- function(d, a, b, what = 'loss') {
  cl[[what]][cl$design == d & abs(cl$c_bm_a - a) < 1e-9 &
               abs(cl$c_bm_b - b) < 1e-9]
}
loss_cr2 <- function(d, a, b) {
  cell(d, 0, a, b, 'E2cr2') - cell(d, 1, a, b, 'E2cr2')
}
monotone_viol <- local({
  n <- 0
  for (m in c('E2', 'E2cr2')) for (d in designs) for (h in hl_main) {
    g <- cs[cs$method == m & cs$design == d & cs$t1half == h, ]
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(g))) for (j in seq_len(nrow(g))) {
      if (i != j && g$c_bm_a[j] >= g$c_bm_a[i] &&
          g$c_bm_b[j] >= g$c_bm_b[i] && g$power[i] > g$power[j]) n <- n + 1
    }
  }
  n
})
dc <- function(h, a, b, m = 'E2') {
  x <- c(CO = cell('CO', h, a, b, m), Hybrid = cell('Hybrid', h, a, b, m),
         OLBDC = cell('OLBDC', h, a, b, m))
  s <- c(CO = cell('CO', h, a, b, m, 'mcse_power'),
         Hybrid = cell('Hybrid', h, a, b, m, 'mcse_power'),
         OLBDC = cell('OLBDC', h, a, b, m, 'mcse_power'))
  list(p = x, s = s)
}
dz <- function(h, a, b, d1, d2, m = 'E2') {
  z <- dc(h, a, b, m)
  sprintf('%s (MCSE %s)', f3(z$p[[d1]] - z$p[[d2]]),
          f3(sqrt(z$s[[d1]]^2 + z$s[[d2]]^2)))
}
```

## Validation gate {#sec-gate}

For the first `r meta$gate_reps` replicates of every design and
half-life, the driver regenerated the four single-channel boundary
cells under the single-encoding DGPs from the same seeds. That gave
`r format(nrow(gate), big.mark = ',')` comparisons. The mean-shift
encoding with weight $a$ was compared with the cell $(a, 0)$, and the
correlation encoding with weight $b$ with the cell $(0, b)$. The
generated data were identical in every comparison, with a largest
absolute difference of `r sprintf('%g', max(gate$max_abs_data_diff))`.
The fitted E2 estimates were identical too, with a largest difference
of `r sprintf('%g', max(gate$max_abs_est_diff, na.rm = TRUE))`. The
gate passed. The boundary cells of the grid are the two single-encoding
DGPs of this driver exactly. Of the `r format(n_fit, big.mark = ',')`
E2 and E2cr2 fits, `r format(n_conv, big.mark = ',')` converged.

## Test calibration under the null

Table \@ref(tab:null) gives the rejection rate in the null cell,
$c_{bm,A} = c_{bm,B} = 0$, with `r n_reps_main` replicates per cell.
The MCSE at the nominal level is `r f3(sqrt(0.05 * 0.95 / n_reps_main))`.
The model-based E2 test rejected at `r nrng('E2', 'CO')` in CO,
`r nrng('E2', 'Hybrid')` in Hybrid and `r nrng('E2', 'OLBDC')` in
OL+BDC. Its size therefore depends on the design. It is slightly
liberal in CO at $t_{1/2} = 1$ week and conservative in OL+BDC at the
same half-life. The calibration ratio $\kappa$ of E2 ranged over
`r krng('E2', 'CO')` in CO, `r krng('E2', 'Hybrid')` in Hybrid and
`r krng('E2', 'OLBDC')` in OL+BDC, across all weight cells. The CR2
test rejected at `r nrng('E2cr2')` in the null cell over all designs
and half-lives. Its $\kappa$ ranged over `r krng('E2cr2')`.

A design-dependent size means that E2 power is not comparable across
designs without qualification. A conservative test loses power, and a
liberal one gains it. Within one design and half-life, the size is
the same for every weight cell, so contrasts between weight cells are
unaffected. We therefore report design comparisons with both tests.

```{r null-table, results = 'asis'}
nt <- nr |>
  dplyr::filter(t1half %in% hl_main) |>
  dplyr::mutate(txt = sprintf('%s (%s)', f3(power), f3(mcse_power))) |>
  dplyr::select(design, t1half, method, txt) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(method, t1half), values_from = txt)
cat('\\begin{table}[H]', '\\small\\centering',
    sprintf(paste0('\\caption{Rejection rate in the null cell ',
                   '($c_{bm,A} = c_{bm,B} = 0$), %d replicates per cell, ',
                   '$N = 70$, MCSE in parentheses. E2 uses the ',
                   'model-based standard error, E2cr2 the CR2 standard ',
                   'error with a Satterthwaite test. Half-lives in ',
                   'weeks.}'), n_reps_main),
    '\\label{tab:null}', '\\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}', '\\toprule',
    '& \\multicolumn{3}{c}{E2} & \\multicolumn{3}{c}{E2cr2} \\\\',
    '\\cmidrule(lr){2-4}\\cmidrule(l){5-7}',
    'Design & $t_{1/2} = 0$ & 0.5 & 1 & $t_{1/2} = 0$ & 0.5 & 1 \\\\',
    '\\midrule', sep = '\n')
for (d in designs) {
  r <- nt[nt$design == d, ]
  cat(sprintf('%s & %s & %s & %s & %s & %s & %s \\\\\n', dname(d),
              r$E2_0, r$E2_0.5, r$E2_1, r$E2cr2_0, r$E2cr2_0.5,
              r$E2cr2_1))
}
cat('\\bottomrule', '\\end{tabular}', '\\end{table}', sep = '\n')
```

## Power over the weight grid

Table \@ref(tab:power-e2) gives E2 power for every cell and Table
\@ref(tab:power-cr2) gives E2cr2 power on the same trials. Power rose
with each weight, holding the other fixed, in every design, half-life
and test. There were `r monotone_viol` exceptions among all ordered
pairs of cells. Monotonicity follows from Equation
\@ref(eq:kappa). Both weights add to the same coefficient with the
same sign. It says nothing about whether the channels act
independently.

At $t_{1/2} = 0$ the two single-channel cells at weight 0.45 had
similar power in every design. Under E2 the values were
`r pw('CO', 0, 0.45, 0)` and `r pw('CO', 0, 0, 0.45)` in CO,
`r pw('Hybrid', 0, 0.45, 0)` and `r pw('Hybrid', 0, 0, 0.45)` in
Hybrid, and `r pw('OLBDC', 0, 0.45, 0)` and `r pw('OLBDC', 0, 0, 0.45)`
in OL+BDC, for the mean-shift and correlation channels in that order.
At $t_{1/2} = 1$ week they separated in Hybrid and OL+BDC (Section
\@ref(sec-eqsum)).

```{r power-e2, results = 'asis'}
cat(power_table('E2', sprintf(paste0(
  'Power of the E2 test (model-based standard error) over the channel ',
  'weights, $N = 70$, %d replicates per cell, MCSE in parentheses. ',
  'Rows give $c_{bm,A}$ (mean-shift channel), columns $c_{bm,B}$ ',
  '(correlation channel). The column $c_{bm,B} = 0$ is the mean-shift ',
  'encoding and the row $c_{bm,A} = 0$ the correlation encoding. ',
  'Half-lives in weeks.'), n_reps_main), 'power-e2'), sep = '\n')
```

```{r power-cr2, results = 'asis'}
cat(power_table('E2cr2', paste0(
  'Power of the E2cr2 test (CR2 standard error, Satterthwaite test) on ',
  'the same trials as Table \\ref{tab:power-e2}. MCSE in ',
  'parentheses.'), 'power-cr2'), sep = '\n')
```

## The fitted coefficient {#sec-est}

At $t_{1/2} = 0$ the fitted coefficient was additive in the two
weights, replicate by replicate. The paired interaction contrast
$\hat\beta(0.45, 0.45) - \hat\beta(0.45, 0) - \hat\beta(0, 0.45) +
\hat\beta(0, 0)$ averaged
`r sprintf('%.1e', max(abs(bench$est_pairs$additivity_dev[bench$est_pairs$t1half == 0])))`
or less in absolute value. The reason is exact. At $t_{1/2} = 0$ the
mean shift is a linear combination of the fixed-effect columns
$B_i D_{bc,it}$ and $D_{bc,it}$. Adding it changes neither the REML
variance estimates nor anything but the interaction estimate. At
$t_{1/2} > 0$ the contrast was at most
`r sprintf('%.1e', max(abs(bench$est_pairs$additivity_dev)))`, against
estimates near `r f2(nominal)` in size.

The two weights did not have equal coefficients at $t_{1/2} > 0$. The
correlation channel's mean estimate stayed within
`r pct(cor_dev)` percent of its nominal value in every design and
half-life. The
mean-shift channel's estimate at weight 0.45 and $t_{1/2} = 1$ week
exceeded the nominal $-`r f3(nominal)`$ by
`r pct(over_sim('CO', 1))` percent in CO,
`r pct(over_sim('Hybrid', 1))` percent in Hybrid and
`r pct(over_sim('OLBDC', 1))` percent in OL+BDC. The MCSE of each mean
estimate was about `r f3(max(cs$mcse_est[cs$method == 'E2']))` or less.
The GLS projection under the true conditional covariance gave
`r pct(kap('CO', 1, 'overshoot_A'))`,
`r pct(kap('Hybrid', 1, 'overshoot_A'))` and
`r pct(kap('OLBDC', 1, 'overshoot_A'))` percent (Section
\@ref(sec-analytic)). The fitted model weights the off-drug visits
differently from the true covariance. Its overshoot was roughly twice
the projection's in Hybrid and three times in OL+BDC. The 2026-10-28
internal review reported 21 to 39 percent for the earlier run, which
lacked the baseline visit and used the original carryover rule. The
direction agrees, and the size depends on the analysis data.

The empirical standard deviation of the E2 estimate exceeded the GLS
standard error under the true covariance in every cell. The ratio of
the two ranged from `r f2(min(sd_ratio))` to `r f2(max(sd_ratio))`.
The working covariance of
the analysis model is a random intercept with continuous AR(1)
errors. The DGP has four correlated components, so the fitted
estimator is less efficient than GLS. The GLS noncentrality therefore
overstates the attainable power and serves as an upper reference only.

## Additivity of power {#sec-additivity}

Table \@ref(tab:additivity) compares the combined cell
$(0.225, 0.225)$ with three benchmarks. The first is the
probability-scale benchmark $p(0.225, 0) + p(0, 0.225) - p(0, 0)$.
The second is the probit benchmark of the 2026-10-28 internal review.
It maps each single-channel power to a noncentrality,
$\hat\Lambda = \Phi^{-1}(\hat\pi) + 1.96$, adds the two and maps back,
$\Phi(\hat\Lambda_A + \hat\Lambda_B - 1.96)$. The third is the same
benchmark with the critical value calibrated to the observed null
rejection rate, $z = \Phi^{-1}(1 - \hat\pi_0/2)$. It corrects for a
test whose size is not 0.05. The table also gives the within-channel
control. It compares $p(0.45, 0)$ with $2p(0.225, 0) - p(0, 0)$ for
the mean-shift channel and the analogous quantity for the correlation
channel.

The combined cell exceeded the probability-scale benchmark by
`r crng('prob_excess_0.225_0.225')` under E2. The single channels
doubled showed the same excess, `r crng('double_A')` for the mean-shift
channel and `r crng('double_B')` for the correlation channel. The
excess is therefore a property of the power curve, not of combining
two channels. At $(0.45, 0.45)$ the probability-scale benchmark
exceeded 1 in every design and half-life. The combined power fell
short of it by `r sprintf('%s to %s', f3(-max(bench$contrasts$value[bench$contrasts$contrast == 'prob_excess_0.450_0.450' & bench$contrasts$method == 'E2' & bench$contrasts$t1half %in% hl_main])), f3(-min(bench$contrasts$value[bench$contrasts$contrast == 'prob_excess_0.450_0.450' & bench$contrasts$method == 'E2' & bench$contrasts$t1half %in% hl_main])))`.

On the probit scale the combined cell agreed with the benchmark. Under
E2 the departure was `r crng('probit_excess_0.225_0.225', c('CO', 'Hybrid'))`
in CO and Hybrid, within about two MCSE in every cell. In OL+BDC it was
`r crng('probit_excess_0.225_0.225', 'OLBDC')`. These are the cells
where E2 was conservative. With the critical value calibrated to the
observed size, the OL+BDC departures were
`r crng('probitcal_excess_0.225_0.225', 'OLBDC')`, and all nine
departures were within two MCSE. Under the CR2 test, whose size was
near nominal, the uncalibrated probit departures were
`r crng('probit_excess_0.225_0.225', m = 'E2cr2')`.
The probit approximation ignores the lower rejection tail and the $t$
reference distribution, so agreement within a few hundredths is what
it can deliver.

```{r additivity-table, results = 'asis'}
cat('\\begin{table}[H]', '\\small\\centering',
    paste0('\\caption{Additivity of E2 power at the combined cell ',
           '$(0.225, 0.225)$ and the within-channel control. Observed: ',
           'power at $(0.225, 0.225)$. Excess over the probability-scale ',
           'benchmark, over the probit benchmark with $z = 1.96$, and ',
           'over the probit benchmark with $z$ calibrated to the observed ',
           'null rejection. Doubling: $p(0.45, 0) - [2p(0.225, 0) - ',
           'p(0, 0)]$ for the mean-shift channel and the same for the ',
           'correlation channel. Paired bootstrap MCSE in parentheses.}'),
    '\\label{tab:additivity}', '\\begin{tabular}{llrrrrrr}', '\\toprule',
    paste0('Design & $t_{1/2}$ & Observed & Prob. & Probit & ',
           'Probit, cal. & Doubling, mean & Doubling, cor. \\\\'),
    '\\midrule', sep = '\n')
for (d in designs) for (h in hl_main) {
  cat(sprintf('%s & %s & %s & %s & %s & %s & %s & %s \\\\\n',
              if (h == 0) dname(d) else '', h,
              f3(cell(d, h, 0.225, 0.225)),
              cv(d, h, 'prob_excess_0.225_0.225'),
              cv(d, h, 'probit_excess_0.225_0.225'),
              cv(d, h, 'probitcal_excess_0.225_0.225'),
              cv(d, h, 'double_A'), cv(d, h, 'double_B')))
}
cat('\\bottomrule', '\\end{tabular}', '\\end{table}', sep = '\n')
```

## The equal-total line and carryover {#sec-eqsum}

The anti-diagonal of the grid holds three pairs with total weight
0.45: $(0.45, 0)$, $(0.225, 0.225)$ and $(0, 0.45)$. On drug they give
the same conditional slope. They differ in the off-drug profile only.
Table \@ref(tab:eqsum) gives their power and the paired difference
between the two single-channel ends.

At $t_{1/2} = 0$ the correlation end had slightly higher power than
the mean-shift end. The paired E2 differences, mean-shift minus
correlation, were `r crng('eqsum_A_minus_B', h = 0)`. This is the
effect of the smaller conditional variance under the correlation
channel. At $t_{1/2} = 1$ week the order reversed in Hybrid and
OL+BDC. The differences were `r cv('Hybrid', 1, 'eqsum_A_minus_B')` and
`r cv('OLBDC', 1, 'eqsum_A_minus_B')`. In CO the difference stayed near
zero, `r cv('CO', 1, 'eqsum_A_minus_B')`. The mixed pair
$(0.225, 0.225)$ lay between the two ends, or within two paired MCSE
of the nearer end, in every design and half-life. Under E2cr2 the reversal at $t_{1/2} = 1$ week was
`r cv('Hybrid', 1, 'eqsum_A_minus_B', 'E2cr2')` in Hybrid and
`r cv('OLBDC', 1, 'eqsum_A_minus_B', 'E2cr2')` in OL+BDC. Pairs with the
same total weight therefore do not give similar power once carryover
is present. The earlier draft stated that they did.

The loss of power from $t_{1/2} = 0$ to 1 week shows the same
difference. Under E2, the mean-shift encoding at weight 0.45 lost
`r f3(loss('Hybrid', 0.45, 0))` in Hybrid and
`r f3(loss('OLBDC', 0.45, 0))` in OL+BDC. The correlation encoding
lost `r f3(loss('Hybrid', 0, 0.45))` and `r f3(loss('OLBDC', 0, 0.45))`.
The MCSE of each loss is about `r f3(max(cl$loss_mcse))`. Under
E2cr2 the losses were `r f3(loss_cr2('Hybrid', 0.45, 0))` and
`r f3(loss_cr2('OLBDC', 0.45, 0))` for the mean-shift encoding and
`r f3(loss_cr2('Hybrid', 0, 0.45))` and `r f3(loss_cr2('OLBDC', 0, 0.45))`
for the correlation encoding. Part of the E2 loss in OL+BDC reflects
the test's growing conservatism there. In CO all losses were small,
`r f3(min(cl$loss[cl$design == 'CO']))` to
`r f3(max(cl$loss[cl$design == 'CO']))` under E2. The correlation
channel's interaction decays with the drug effect. The mean-shift
channel's interaction stops at discontinuation, so the off-drug
visits keep their contrast with the on-drug visits. The earlier draft
stated that the two channels contribute comparably to carryover
sensitivity. In the Hybrid and OL+BDC designs the correlation channel
lost more than twice as much power under either test.

```{r eqsum-table, results = 'asis'}
cat('\\begin{table}[H]', '\\small\\centering',
    paste0('\\caption{Power along the equal-total line ',
           '$c_{bm,A} + c_{bm,B} = 0.45$, E2 and E2cr2, MCSE in ',
           'parentheses. Difference: power at $(0.45, 0)$ minus power at ',
           '$(0, 0.45)$, paired, with bootstrap MCSE. Half-lives in ',
           'weeks.}'),
    '\\label{tab:eqsum}', '\\begin{tabular}{lllrrrr}', '\\toprule',
    paste0('Design & $t_{1/2}$ & Test & $(0.45, 0)$ & $(0.225, 0.225)$ & ',
           '$(0, 0.45)$ & Difference \\\\'),
    '\\midrule', sep = '\n')
for (d in designs) for (h in hl_main) for (m in c('E2', 'E2cr2')) {
  ps <- function(a, b) sprintf('%s (%s)', f3(cell(d, h, a, b, m)),
                               f3(cell(d, h, a, b, m, 'mcse_power')))
  cat(sprintf('%s & %s & %s & %s & %s & %s & %s \\\\\n',
              if (h == 0 && m == 'E2') dname(d) else '',
              if (m == 'E2') h else '', m, ps(0.45, 0), ps(0.225, 0.225),
              ps(0, 0.45), cv(d, h, 'eqsum_A_minus_B', m)))
}
cat('\\bottomrule', '\\end{tabular}', '\\end{table}', sep = '\n')
```

The ranking of designs depended on the channel and the half-life. The
Hybrid design had the highest power, or power within two MCSE of the
highest, in every single-channel cell at weight 0.45 under both
tests. At weight 0.225 and $t_{1/2} = 1$ week, CO exceeded Hybrid on
the correlation channel under E2,
`r dz(1, 0, 0.225, 'CO', 'Hybrid')`, but not under E2cr2,
`r dz(1, 0, 0.225, 'CO', 'Hybrid', 'E2cr2')`. That E2 difference
reflects the liberal E2 test in CO. The order of CO and OL+BDC was not fixed. At
$t_{1/2} = 0$ and weight 0.45 on the correlation channel, OL+BDC
exceeded CO by `r dz(0, 0, 0.45, 'OLBDC', 'CO', 'E2cr2')` under E2cr2.
At $t_{1/2} = 1$ week the difference was
`r dz(1, 0, 0.45, 'OLBDC', 'CO', 'E2cr2')`. On the mean-shift channel
at $t_{1/2} = 1$ week, OL+BDC exceeded CO by
`r dz(1, 0.45, 0, 'OLBDC', 'CO', 'E2cr2')`. Under E2 the CO and OL+BDC
differences also carry the two tests' different sizes. The earlier
draft stated that the design ranking was preserved throughout the
grid. For CO and OL+BDC it is not.

```{r g9-hl02, child = 'results-extra.Rmd'}
```
